items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source (Unauthenticated Customer Account Takeover)
items.summary: Adobe released a security update addressing seven vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-71362, a critical unauthenticated customer account takeover with a CVSS score of 9.1. This flaw allows attackers to switch customer sessions and access private data without credentials or admin privileges.

items.title: Security update for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source (Unauthenticated Arbitrary Code Execution via Webhooks)
items.summary: Adobe published a bulletin covering 13 vulnerabilities, with CVE-2026-48358 rated CVSS 10.0. This critical flaw in the webhooks component allows unauthenticated, zero-interaction arbitrary code execution.

items.title: Unauthenticated File Upload in Amasty Order Attributes for Magento
items.summary: An unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability in Amasty Order Attributes allows attackers to write executable files to a Magento store without logging in, potentially leading to remote code execution. Amasty has released patches for this and other critical vulnerabilities in their extensions.

items.title: Critical vulnerability in Mirasvit Cache Warmer for Magento (Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection)
items.summary: Sansec discovered an unauthenticated PHP object injection vulnerability in Mirasvit Cache Warmer, a popular Magento extension. A crafted cookie on any storefront page can lead to remote code execution (CVSS 9.8).

items.title: PolyShell: unrestricted file upload in Magento and Adobe Commerce
items.summary: Sansec discovered PolyShell, a critical flaw in Magento's REST API that allows unauthenticated attackers to upload executable files using a polyglot technique. Attacks have been observed on a significant percentage of stores.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce
items.summary: Adobe released a security update for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source, resolving critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities. Successful exploitation could lead to arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, and security feature bypass.
